backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 linearly up to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param group before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Change only MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.025. Keep every other hyperparameter, including the warmdown schedule and WEIGHT_DECAY, identical so the result isolates the matrix learning rate.
backlog.title: Muon learning-rate sweep (lower)

backlog.spec: Scale each Muon orthogonalized update by 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols)) instead of the current shape factor, so the update RMS matches AdamW's typical magnitude and one shared learning rate transfers across matrix shapes. Retune nothing else; keep MATRIX_LR as the base learning rate.
backlog.title: Muon update shape scaling (Moonlight-style)

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This saves optimizer compute per step, which buys more training steps in the fixed 300 s window. Keep the quintic coefficients as they are, or use the standard Muon coefficients for the chosen iteration count.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Disable Nesterov momentum in the Muon update (use the plain momentum buffer as the update direction) to test whether the simpler update helps at this scale. Change only the nesterov flag and leave momentum and learning rates alone.
backlog.title: Nesterov toggle off for Muon

backlog.spec: Set the first Adam beta (beta1) to 0.9 for the embedding, lm_head, and per-layer scalar parameter groups while keeping beta2 at 0.95. Muon parameters are unchanged. This tests whether a slower first-moment average stabilizes the high embedding and scalar learning rates.
backlog.title: Adam beta1 for embeddings and scalars

backlog.spec: Exclude the token embedding and lm_head parameters from weight decay (set their decay to 0) while keeping WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 on Muon matrix parameters. Embeddings often do not benefit from decay and this avoids shrinking the high-LR embedding rows.
backlog.title: Separate weight decay for embeddings

backlog.spec: Change only WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 for the Muon matrix parameters. Keep all learning rates and schedules identical so the effect of decay strength on the 300 s run can be read directly.
backlog.title: Weight decay sweep

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the linear LR decay covers the last 70 percent of the time budget. Keep the warmup at zero and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. This tests whether a longer anneal to zero improves the final validation loss.
backlog.title: Warmdown length extension

backlog.spec: Replace the linear LR decay in the warmdown phase with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the warmdown window, computed from elapsed time over the budget. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5 and all peak learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so every learning rate ramps linearly from zero over the first 2 percent of the time budget before following the existing warmdown. This guards the high embedding and scalar learning rates against early instability.
backlog.title: Short warmup before peak LR

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10 percent of the peak learning rate rather than at zero. Keep all other schedule settings unchanged. This checks whether a nonzero final LR helps the last steps on this short run.
backlog.title: Final LR floor at 10 percent

backlog.spec: Replace the warmdown curve with lr = peak * (1 - t)^0.5 over the warmdown window, where t is the fraction of warmdown elapsed, ending at FINAL_LR_FRAC. The longer tail at high LR may keep the model learning longer than linear decay does.
backlog.title: Sqrt-decay warmdown

backlog.spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step uses about 262K tokens. Under a fixed 300 s clock this gives roughly twice as many optimizer steps, which may matter more than per-step gradient quality for a small model. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic consistent with the new total.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch for more steps

backlog.spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 so each step uses about 1M tokens. Keep the learning rates unchanged and let the existing gradient accumulation absorb the larger batch. This tests the opposite trade-off, lower gradient noise at fewer steps.
backlog.title: Larger total batch

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to output logits before the cross-entropy loss: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). Apply it in the forward pass for both training and evaluation paths in the model code, without changing the evaluation call itself. This bounds logit magnitude and can stabilize training at high learning rates.
backlog.title: Logit softcapping

backlog.spec: Apply RMSNorm (no learned gain) to the query and key vectors per head before the attention dot product. This keeps attention logits bounded so the high Muon and embedding learning rates do not blow up attention entropy. Keep the rest of the attention block unchanged.
backlog.title: QK normalization in attention

backlog.spec: Keep a copy x0 of the normalized token embedding after the embedding layer. At the start of each block, mix the current residual stream with x0 using a learnable per-layer scalar pair (a, b) initialized to (1, 0), computed as x = a * x + b * x0. This gives every layer direct access to the input token identity.
backlog.title: Initial-embedding residual skip

backlog.spec: Change the rotary position embedding base from 10000 to 100000. The larger base gives lower-frequency components more range, which can help the sliding-window and full-attention layers on the 300 s run. Leave the head dimension and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: RoPE base frequency change

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so each attention layer has twice as many heads at the same model width. Keep the model dimension unchanged. This tests whether finer-grained heads help at this small scale.
backlog.title: Head dimension 64

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so the model width stays near 480 while the layer count increases. Keep HEAD_DIM and all optimizer settings as they are. This trades width for depth under the same time budget.
backlog.title: Deeper, narrower model

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to full-context attention on every layer (for example "LLLL"-style behavior for all DEPTH layers). The sequences are short enough that the half-context sliding layers may be losing useful context, and removing them might lower validation bpb even if each step is slightly slower.
backlog.title: Sliding window pattern all full attention

backlog.spec: After the token embedding, add a learned gate-weighted copy of the previous token's embedding to each position, with the first position receiving no addition. Use a single learnable scalar gate initialized near zero so the model starts close to the baseline. This gives cheap local context at the input.
backlog.title: Previous-token bigram mixing at input

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block so attention and the MLP both read the same normalized input and their outputs are summed into the residual, instead of applying the MLP after attention. This reduces sequential ops per layer and can speed up each step on the A100 within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP block

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to zeros so every residual branch starts as identity at step zero. Keep other initializations unchanged. This commonly stabilizes early training when the learning rates are large.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized output projections

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the cross-entropy loss over the output logits to keep the normalization constant near zero. Apply the term to training loss only and keep the reported validation computation unchanged. This discourages logit drift at high learning rates.
backlog.title: Attention logit z-loss regularizer

backlog.spec: Add no dropout anywhere in the model, and remove any existing dropout if present, to confirm that the short 300 s run is underfit and does not benefit from regularization. Make no other change. This acts as a control on whether regularization is wasting capacity.
backlog.title: Embedding dropout or none check

backlog.spec: Maintain an EMA of all trainable parameters with decay 0.999 updated every step. Evaluate using the EMA weights at the end of training by swapping them in before the harness evaluation path runs. Do not alter the evaluation call or summary printing; only swap the parameter values beforehand.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights

backlog.spec: Speed up the optimizer by batching Muon's Newton-Schulz step across matrix parameters with identical shapes (stack them and orthogonalize together) rather than looping one matrix at a time. Results should match the current optimizer up to numerical noise, and the saved time increases the number of steps in the 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Fused or faster optimizer step

backlog.spec: Train with shorter sequences in the first 30 percent of the time budget, for example half the usual context length with twice the batch in sequences, then switch to full context for the rest. Keep the tokens per optimizer step identical. This may speed early learning and reduces attention cost early on.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Keep the model and optimizer unchanged, but grow the effective batch over the 300 s budget. Start at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/4 for the first 30% of elapsed time, move to TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/2 until 60%, then use the full TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE. Implement this by changing the number of gradient-accumulation micro-steps per optimizer step, computed from elapsed time each step. Scale the loss by the micro-step count as the existing code does, so gradients stay on the same scale. Leave the seed lines, the evaluation call and the summary printing untouched.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp during the run

backlog.spec: Before each optimizer step, clip the global gradient norm across all trainable parameters to 1.0 using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_. Apply it after backward and before the Muon and Adam steps. This adds no new hyperparameter beyond the threshold constant. It guards against the occasional large-gradient spikes that high LRs such as EMBEDDING_LR=0.6 can produce.
backlog.title: Global gradient-norm clipping

backlog.spec: During training only, randomly skip each transformer block's attention and MLP residual contribution per example with a drop probability that rises linearly with depth, from 0 at layer 0 to 0.1 at the last layer. Rescale kept branches by 1/(1-p) as in standard DropPath. Disable it at evaluation. This is a regularizer aimed at the small-model regime, where it may slightly hurt, so it is a bold test of whether extra regularization pays off under a fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on residual branches

backlog.spec: Split the DEPTH layers into an encoder half and a decoder half. Save each encoder layer's output hidden state, and in the decoder add it back to the input of the mirrored layer through a learned per-channel scalar initialized to 0. Use the existing per-layer scalar parameters for the new weights so no new optimizer group is needed. This gives the decoder direct access to earlier-layer features and is a larger architectural change than the residual tweaks already tried.
backlog.title: U-Net-style long skip connections

backlog.spec: After scaled dot-product attention and before the output projection, multiply each head's output by a sigmoid gate computed from the block input through a small linear layer of size n_heads. Initialize that linear layer's weights to zero and its bias so the gate starts near 0.5 at the start of training. The gate gives the model per-head control over how much each head contributes. Keep the rest of the attention path, including the sliding-window pattern, unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid output gate on attention

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP in each block with a SwiGLU MLP. Use a gate projection and an up projection, each mapping model_dim to hidden size round(8/3 * model_dim) rounded to a multiple of 64, followed by SiLU(gate) times up, then the down projection back to model_dim. This keeps the parameter count roughly equal to the existing 4x MLP. Keep the Muon grouping rule so all new matrices are still orthogonalized.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count

backlog.spec: Apply rotary position embedding to only the first half of each attention head's channels, and leave the second half unrotated so it can carry position-free content. Keep the same RoPE base and head dimension. This is a one-line change inside the function that applies rotary embeddings to q and k. It tests whether a mix of positional and non-positional channels helps a small byte-level-trained model.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embedding on half of head dimensions

backlog.spec: Move the token embedding and lm_head weight matrices out of the Adam groups and into the Muon group, so their updates are Newton-Schulz orthogonalized like the hidden matrices. Use MATRIX_LR for both. Keep the Adam learning rates for the remaining scalar and norm parameters. This is a bold optimizer test: Muon-style updates on the embedding may change the effective learning rate for rare tokens and interact with the Adam betas. Keep the rest of setup_optimizer unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon orthogonalized updates for embedding and LM head

backlog.spec: Scale the Adam learning rates for the embedding, lm_head and scalar groups by base_width/model_dim, where base_width is 256, so that wider or narrower configurations keep comparable effective step sizes. Leave MATRIX_LR and the Muon path untouched. Set the scale factor once in setup_optimizer from the model dimension, with no other tuning. This is a small, self-contained learning-rate-transfer test.
backlog.title: Width-scaled Adam learning rates

backlog.spec: Build the attention mask so tokens cannot attend across document boundaries inside a packed sequence. Detect boundaries using the document-separator token id that the training batches already carry, using only names already imported from prepare.py; do not read prepare.py internals. Combine this with the existing causal and sliding-window mask. Compute the boundary mask once per batch and reuse it across layers. This reduces cross-document noise in packed training sequences.
backlog.title: Document-boundary attention masking

backlog.spec: In CausalSelfAttention.forward, save the value tensor v produced by the first transformer block and, in every later block, replace v with (1 - lam) * v + lam * v_first, where lam is a new per-layer learnable scalar initialized to 0.5 and kept in the scalar Adam group (SCALAR_LR). Leave the first block unchanged. No other hyperparameters change. This is the ResFormer-style value residual that lets deeper layers reuse first-layer value features.
backlog.title: Value residual from first layer

backlog.spec: Change the attention so there are N_HEAD query heads but only 2 key/value heads, with each KV head shared across N_HEAD/2 query heads (repeat_interleave K and V before the attention call, or use enable_gqa in scaled_dot_product_attention). Keep HEAD_DIM and model_dim unchanged, so the k/v projection matrices shrink and the step gets cheaper. The aim is more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s budget, which has been the main lever so far. Keep the sliding-window pattern as is.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with 2 KV heads

backlog.spec: Set the lm_head weight to the same Parameter object as the token embedding (wte.weight), so the two share storage. Drop the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR Adam group and put the shared tensor in the EMBEDDING_LR group. Scale the logits by a fixed 1/sqrt(model_dim) before the softcap-free head so the shared weight's scale is reasonable. This removes about 50% of the vocab-sized parameters and frees parameter budget for width, with no other change to the model.
backlog.title: Tie input embedding and LM head

backlog.spec: Keep the total number of block applications at DEPTH but store only DEPTH//2 distinct transformer blocks. The forward pass applies the block list twice in sequence, with the second pass using the same weights and a learned per-pass scalar gate initialized to 1 on the residual branch. Optimizer parameter groups should deduplicate the shared tensors so each is updated once. Widen model_dim by about 1.2x (keeping HEAD_DIM) to use the freed parameters. This is a bolder test of whether compute per parameter beats parameter count under a fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Looped shared-weight block recurrence

backlog.spec: Add one extra linear head that predicts the token two steps ahead (t+2) from the same final hidden states. Compute its cross-entropy against targets shifted by two, and add it to the main loss with weight 0.3. Use the same optimizer group as lm_head (Adam at UNEMBEDDING_LR). At eval time use only the main next-token head, so the harness evaluation path is untouched. The extra supervision is meant to make each step more informative.
backlog.title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head

backlog.spec: The metric is bits per byte, but training uses per-token cross-entropy, which over-weights short tokens relative to the metric. Compute a per-token byte-length weight w_t = bytes(token_t) / mean bytes per token in the batch, where byte lengths come from a lookup table built once at startup by decoding each vocabulary id from the tokenizer object already used in train.py (do not read prepare.py internals). Multiply the per-token loss by w_t before averaging, then normalize by the sum of w_t. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy

backlog.spec: Replace the single linear warmdown with a two-cycle schedule over the time budget. Cycle 1 holds the peak LR for the first 40% of elapsed time, then cosine-decays to 0.3 of peak by 60%. Cycle 2 jumps back to peak, holds until 75%, then cosine-decays to 0 at 100%. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups, and keep the Muon momentum schedule unchanged. The goal is to test whether a warm restart gives a better final basin than one long warmdown.
backlog.title: Two-cycle cosine schedule with mid-run restart

backlog.spec: Speed up each step without changing the math. Replace any explicit attention mask construction with F.scaled_dot_product_attention using is_causal=True on full-context layers, and for sliding-window layers use the flash/mem-efficient kernel with a precomputed boolean mask cached once per (seq_len, window) pair. Enable torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and cudnn.allow_tf32. Keep torch.compile but use mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' if compile time stays under 60 s. Log tokens per second at the first step so the gain can be checked. The purpose is more tokens processed in the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Throughput pass: SDPA flash path and CUDA graphs

backlog.spec: As a light regularizer, during training only, replace each input token independently with a random vocabulary id with probability 0.03, while keeping the unchanged target tokens as the labels. Apply this to the input embedding lookup only, and disable it when the model is in eval mode. Sample the replacement mask with torch.rand each step using the existing generator. Keep all optimizer settings unchanged. This is a bolder data-side regularizer aimed at the small-model overfit regime, and it should not alter the eval path.
backlog.title: Stochastic input-token span corruption

backlog.spec: Modify the Muon step so that after the Newton-Schulz orthogonalized update is computed, each element of the update whose sign disagrees with the sign of the current raw gradient is zeroed out (the cautious masking rule), and the remaining elements are rescaled by numel/(number of kept elements) so the average update norm stays the same. Apply this only to the matrix parameter group. Keep the existing weight decay and learning rates unchanged. This is a bolder optimizer variant that could reduce noisy steps late in training.
backlog.title: Sign-consistency masking on Muon updates

incumbent.description: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to increase optimizer steps under the fixed time budget, potentially improving convergence for a small model.

memo: Incumbent is 1.0989 (slot 8, halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, -0.0156), the only accept. More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s helped most. Doubling the batch hurt badly (+0.0816), which agrees with that. Neutral or worse: MATRIX_LR 0.025 (+0.0066), 10 layers (+0.0189), window "L" (+0.0017), WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1 (+0.0002), the previous-token gate (+0.0035), EMA (+0.0012), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0001), SwiGLU (+0.0001). Some later results look better than the incumbent but were rejected: grad clipping (1.0921/1.0911, -0.0073), the Muon update scaling (1.0933, -0.0056) and the value residual (1.0955, -0.0033). Their deltas may have been measured against a different baseline, so re-check them. Next: halve the batch again; re-run the incumbent to measure noise; re-test clipping, the Muon scaling, value residual, FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.1 and the curriculum on the new incumbent, alone and combined; try a higher MATRIX_LR; fix the two patch_fail edits (Newton-Schulz 3 iterations, embedding weight decay).
